meta.name: Pony Beads (9mm)
meta.description: Because of their size, these beads are easy to work with and are useful for large banners and fun for kids projects.

meta.name: Toho Aiko
meta.description: Aiko Beads are top-quality beads manufactured with state-of-the art machinery. Since they are very consistent in shape and size and the resulting beaded piece has a smooth, silken finish.

meta.name: Toho Treasures
meta.description: These beads are not as precise as the Toho Aiko but much more uniform than any other Rocailles.

meta.name: Toho Rounds
meta.description: This line of beads from Toho are similar to Delica Rocailles. They are more rounded and not as uniform in size or shape as precision cylinder beads.

meta.name: Preciosa Rocialles (Size 11)
meta.description: These traditional seed beads from the Czech Republic are similar in shape to Miyuki Rocialles.

meta.name: Generic Colors
meta.description: These colors do not represent any brand of bead and are used for matching up closest colors while stitching your design together.

meta.name: Miyuki Delicas (Size 10)
meta.description: Size 10 Delicas have the same Miyuki precision but are smaller than 8/0 and larger than 11/0.

meta.name: Miyuki Delicas (Size 11)
meta.description: Arguably the most popular brand and size bead for most beaders. They cost more than rocailles but are also more uniform in size and shape.

meta.name: Miyuki Delicas (Size 15)
meta.description: These beads are significantly smaller than 11/0 Delicas and have fewer colors to choose from.

meta.name: Miyuki Delicas (Size 8)
meta.description: These are currently the largest Delicas Miyuki makes.

meta.name: 10th Mountain Division
meta.description: 10th Mountain Division - 2nd Batallion / 87th Infantry Regiment. Fort Drum, New York.

meta.name: Butterfly
meta.description: These butterfly halves are meant to serve as a template. Change the colors to your liking and then copy, mirror and paste to create a complete butterfly.

meta.name: USA Flag
meta.description: The flag of the United States of America.

meta.name: International Karate Plus
meta.description: A screenshot from a very old game created for the Commodore 64. One of my favorites!

meta.name: Apple Tree 4
meta.description: This Apple Tree pattern has been with us since BeadTool 2. This version has been updated with a better color selection than the previous ones. If you are the original author, please contact me!

meta.name: Just the Bead Chart
meta.description: This layout will only print the name of your pattern and the Bead Chart on a single page.

meta.name: Bead Chart and Legend
meta.description: This layout will only print the Bead Chart and the accompanying Bead Legend on a single page.

meta.name: Full Printout
meta.description: This layout will print the Bead Chart and Bead Legend on a single page PLUS a Word Chart starting on the 2nd page.

meta.name: Just the Pattern
meta.description: This layout will show a realistic view of what the pattern might look like when stitched up. The actual bead size will not be reproduced.

meta.name: Large Pattern
meta.description: This layout is meant for very large patterns and includes the Bead Legend, Bead Chart and Word Chart. It will fill as many pages as necessary.

meta.name: Extended Printout
meta.description: This layout is similar to the Full Printout but includes a little more information about the pattern and changes the location of the Bead Legend.

meta.name: 2 Column Split
meta.description: This layout features a 2 column split Bead Graph and is useful for patterns that are tall and skinny.

meta.name: 3 Column Split
meta.description: This layout features a 3 column split Bead Graph and is useful for patterns that are tall and skinny.

meta.name: 2 Row Split
meta.description: This layout features a 2 row split Bead Graph and is useful for patterns that are wide and short.

meta.name: 3 Row Split
meta.description: This layout features a 3 row split Bead Graph and is useful for patterns that are wide and short.

tips.tip: You don't have to close BeadTool to start a new pattern. Just click File->New from the main menu.
Right clicking on a color in your Bead List will bring up some nifty options.
You can get help at any time by clicking Help->Documentation from the main menu.
You can create your own custom palettes by clicking on Tools->My Palettes from the main menu.
To save all the colors in your Bead List as a custom palette just click File->Export->Bead List from the main menu.
You can delete all instances of a single color by right clicking on a color in your Bead List and selecting the Erase option.
Right clicking on a color in your pattern will select that color for drawing.
The developer of BeadTool is only an email away! Just visit www.beadtool.net
It's a good idea to keep your copy of BeadTool up to date!
If you don't like what your printouts look like just click File->Print Preview and choose a different layout.
You can export your patterns as pictures for sharing. Just click File->Export->Pattern from the main menu.
Moving the pattern or picture even slightly can give different results during the transfer.
Changing the brightness & contrast of your picture before loading it will give drastically different results when transferring.
Egyptian burial sites have yielded enormous quantities of beads. They were commonly worn to protect the wearer from misfortune rather than to express status or wealth.
From 1830-1850, the tiniest beads included sizes 20/0 and smaller. These small size beads are no longer made because the process is too labor intensive.
The Egyptian word for luck was "SHA", and "SHA SHA" came to be the word for bead.
During the 2 week Mardi Gras holiday in New Orleans, it's customary for women to "flash" the bead bearer in exchange for a string of cheap plastic beads.
Egyptians were making glass beads by 1365 B.C.
There are several thousand year old glass factories in Lebanon that are still in production.
